rules.note: Aeson encodes JSON objects and transports append LF. TLS splits on LF; Handle getLine APIs hide terminator status, so explicit rejection of partial final EOF frames is not established. Aeson validates UTF-8 while decoding.
No 65,535-byte final send checks. TCP/Stdio hGetLine/getLine are unbounded; TLS concatenates its IORef buffer without a cap until LF. Applies to CLI and public library.
FromJSON dispatches proto_step and required fields while ignoring additive outer object keys.
Each replay, validation, generation and exploration helper sends registration first. Existing-job controls do not register.

Stepping returns immediately on mismatch and terminal errors; no further internal flow writes. Reusing caller-owned transport is caller responsibility. Shared C5 async registration wording conflicts with guide section 10 and server behavior.

The validate CLI brackets transport with tcpClose/tlsClose and maps EOF/errors to exit 2. Library ownership remains caller-managed. tlsClose sends best-effort bye; underlying socket release is documented at process exit.
No protocol heartbeat or idle deadline assumed by the client library; blocking await supports indefinite waits.
InitialState/NextStep dispatches the handler, sends exactly one ReportState, then waits for StepOk or mismatch.
Application clientHandler returns the full observable Map. Arbitrary observation fidelity remains application responsibility.
handleStep returns Left on StepMismatch immediately without waiting for AllStepsDone. Historical Haskell SERVER trailing-done behavior is not a client defect.
Unbounded Integer is emitted as #bigint decimal; integral JSON numbers are accepted. Malformed ITF defense was not freshly verified.
stepLoop is message-driven, without hardcoded step counts.

CLI reads root spec plus explicit --dep files only. It does not advertise automatic recursive resolution. Caller must include the full EXTENDS/INSTANCE closure. The complete send still lacks C2 bounds.
Existing Haskell optional encoders send null or omit by message, per the documented oracle asymmetry.
--cinit propagates constInit; caller selects a valid initializer for CONSTANTS.
Bound is passed to registration with no local cap. Server rejects out-of-range values synchronously; this rule does not require local validation.
IDs can cross connections, but poll/await/cancel discard returned IDs. Submission also ignores accepted kind. A foreign outcome can be associated with the requested job.
awaitJob preserves optional timeout and re-awaits nonterminal status. A terminal status without result makes one final poll, then errors.

Explicit cancel helper accepts only JobStatus, whereas guide reply grammar also permits JobResult. Both current Haskell and Lean servers return status on cancel; no current-server failure is asserted.
runClientValidateAsync unwraps JobValidateDone into the same ValidateResult as sync. Infrastructure errors remain errors.
Unknown causes one extra query and then terminal error. There is no indefinite unknown retry loop expecting the job to appear.
No automatic pool. register_error maps to Left, including a full queue. Applications own connection limits.
No explicit completion ordering assumption, but dropping returned IDs fails to correlate independent jobs. See C17 finding.
TLS13 is the only supported version; client credentials and CA are loaded; certificate-request hook returns the credential.

Uses defaultParamsClient host with CA. No explicit SAN-only policy hook is present. Dependency implementation is unavailable locally; CN-only rejection is not established. Wildcard differences are documented.

Peer SHA256 pin is checked before protocol but compared as case-sensitive Text. Uppercase valid pins fail. Guide section 10 explicitly records this Haskell difference. Explicit registry pin precedence is correct.
POSIX check forbids only group/other access (077). It accepts 0400, 0700 and special bits rather than literal 0600. Windows ACL exception is explicit.
Historical reference client advertises legacy protocol only; no compiled verification or descriptor API.
No native Haskell Gate control facade is advertised.

findings.trigger: Send an encoded registration/state above 65,535 bytes, or receive an unterminated peer line growing beyond the limit.
findings.impact: Oversized output reaches the Lean server and fails; malicious or misconfigured peers can grow receive memory without bound before JSON parsing.
findings.confidence: high; source-confirmed, no fresh runtime probe
findings.fix: Centralize final encoded send validation and use bounded raw-byte JSONL readers before Aeson. Test exact ASCII/multibyte boundaries and oversized unterminated lines.

findings.trigger: A query/await/cancel for job A receives JobStatus/JobResult for job B, or a validation submission receives a gen-traces acceptance.
findings.impact: Public helpers accept unrelated status/outcome; validation can report another job verdict. Conforming servers normally echo the ID, so this is a defensive protocol-failure path.
findings.confidence: high; source-confirmed, malformed-peer path not freshly probed
findings.fix: Compare every returned job ID with the requested ID and require the expected accepted kind. Return a protocol error without continuing on a mismatch.

findings.trigger: A valid client key has mode 0400, 0700, or special bits with no group/other access.
findings.impact: Accepted modes violate the literal 0600 guide contract. No confidentiality exposure is claimed for owner-only access.
findings.confidence: high; source-confirmed, no exact-context runtime probe
findings.fix: Choose exact 0600 enforcement or document the intended private-only policy. Exact enforcement should compare mode & 07777 with 0600.

findings.trigger: A legal peer answers cancel_job with a matching terminal job_result.
findings.impact: cancelJob returns UnexpectedMessage instead of accepting the acknowledgement. Current Haskell and Lean servers return JobStatus, so this is a grammar compatibility gap rather than a current-server regression.
findings.confidence: high; source-confirmed acceptance subset, current server path unaffected
findings.fix: Accept matching JobResult as a terminal acknowledgement, preserving ID correlation and malformed-reply failure.

testEvidence.cases: Mock correct replay, mismatch, canned/fixed and invalid spec. HourClock case invokes model operations and was not run.
Normal transport, bigint state and drop survival. No 65k boundary cases found.
Normal mTLS, wrong CA/pin and discovery. CN-only client rejection and uppercase pin acceptance not established.
Production store/server async lifecycle and unknown IDs. Not fresh malformed-reply acceptance of public client helpers.

limits: Read-only source audit. No builds, tests, probes, live peers or model operations invoked.
Haskell reference is a historical oracle, not a newly qualified framework profile or current package acceptance.
Haskell SERVER trailing AllStepsDone after mismatch and stdio async error-tag differences are not client bugs.
Case-sensitive C26 pin comparison is an explicitly documented reference exception. Lowercase pins work and wrong pins fail before protocol.
C25 SAN-only behavior needs dependency-source inspection or a CN-only certificate fixture; no CN fallback defect is asserted.
Complete inline dependency closure, CONSTANTS initializer, observation fidelity and transport ownership remain caller responsibilities.
MI and Gate SO profiles are not advertised.
